text:
The government is considering sending unannounced disaster alert messages during this week's annual college entrance exam to catch cheaters using their phones and prevent artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating, an interior ministry official said Wednesday.
Authorities have been mulling measures to root out cheating during the College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT) on Thursday following a recent cheating scandal in the certified tax accountant exam using AI.
As part of anti-cheating measures unveiled Tuesday, the government said it would send an emergency alert message, designed to reach most mobile phones and sound a loud alarm even when muted, before the start of the exam to detect any unsubmitted devices.
The official said the government is considering sending alerts unannounced in addition to the planned alert scheduled to be sent between 8:25 and 8:30 a.m.
"If the time is known, there would effectively be no point in additional alerts," the official said.
President Lee Jae Myung said Tuesday he had instructed authorities to review sending additional alerts, even during testing, to catch cheaters.
South Korea has recently been rocked by the recent confession of the top scorer in this year's certified tax accountant exam that he had cheated with the help of AI and digital devices.
The incident has deepened worries of such cheating on the upcoming CSAT, widely seen as major life event in South Korea where the university one goes to can heavily influence career prospects.
